answer: A gale of cheap fake identities collapses when every agent must stake scarce reputation earned through verified work, not just a new keypair. Newcomers start on shale-thin trust: tiny limits and slow-growing credit that only real, attested transactions thicken over time. An ivory-tower whitelist alone fails, so peers cross-check behavior, stake, and history before granting economic weight, making a thousand sock puppets cost far more than they can ever earn.
